subject.title: [Bug]: cron.remove does not clean up session records in sessions.json

question: Should deleted cron jobs purge their base session rows immediately during `cron.remove`, or should deleted-job base rows be removed only through guarded retention cleanup?
rationale: Current main leaves the rows, while related cleanup work shows live base rows can preserve model/auth/label choices; the permanent cleanup boundary needs maintainer intent before another autonomous fix lane is safe.

options.title: Split Delete And Retention Scopes
options.body: Land or revise the guarded retention work for stale orphan rows, then add a narrow immediate `cron.remove` cleanup only if maintainers require deleted jobs to disappear from session UI immediately.

options.title: Immediate Delete Cleanup
options.body: Make `cron.remove` purge the deleted job's base and run session rows with tests for active runs, per-agent stores, and carried preferences.

options.title: Retention-Only Cleanup
options.body: Accept that deleted-job base rows are removed after `cron.sessionRetention` and document that immediate Control UI disappearance is not guaranteed.

recommendation.title: Split Delete And Retention Scopes
recommendation.body: Land or revise the guarded retention work for stale orphan rows, then add a narrow immediate `cron.remove` cleanup only if maintainers require deleted jobs to disappear from session UI immediately.

likelyOwner.reason: openperf owns the active overlapping PR that maintainers need to accept, revise, or split from immediate delete cleanup.
